notes.text: Two things nobody has confirmed: Round1 DiverCity's year-end hours and Gabuu's closing days. Check both this morning before you build the night around them.
Original passports on everyone all day: tax-free at every shop, the morning highball, and Round1's age check tonight.
Cold December day that goes dark around sunset at Shiba Park. Layer up for the street stools and the tower; Ameyoko and Daitoryo want cash.

stops.summary: Tokyo's year-end market at full roar: graze breakfast down the alley and haggle for New Year snacks.
stops.story: Dec 28 is the week Ameyoko turns into a shoving, shouting year-end buying rush, with whole Tokyo families hauling crab and New Year food under the train tracks. Stallholders bark prices, the chocolate guy throws in extra if you play along, and breakfast is whatever is on a stick in front of you. It is chaos, and it is the most Tokyo morning you will get.
how: Split into pairs and graze: fruit skewers, crab, the shouting chocolate stall.
Haggle for New Year snacks to take home.
Regroup at Ueno Station's Shinobazu exit, then walk 2 min up the alley to Daitoryo.
tips: Fix the meet-up point before you split: phones get useless in this crush.
Cash is king here; small notes make haggling faster.
Hours vary shop by shop, so if a stall you want is shuttered, move on.
wishes: Streetwear, sneakers and vintage (Harajuku, Koenji, Shimokitazawa, Ameyoko, Amerikamura), Don Quijote and tax-free hauls
We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.summary: Highballs before noon on street stools under the tracks while the year-end crowd surges past.
stops.story: Daitoryo is Ameyoko's famous motsu-yaki joint, open-fronted and pouring from 10:00, with skewers from about ¥100–200. It is one round, a few sticks of offal grilled over the coals, and the smug feeling of drinking in public at breakfast. This is the story you tell first.
how: Grab whatever stools are free; expect to split 4+4.
One highball each plus a few skewers, then go.
Walk to JR Ueno for the train to Akihabara: 24 min door to door, ¥160, or a 6 min taxi.
tips: They split groups when it is full; take the split rather than wait.
Some foreign visitors in 2024–25 felt they were seated slower; if the wait drags, try Uokusa's standing seafood bar instead.
Drinking age is 20: have the passports ready.
stops.cost: About ¥1,000 pp for a drink and skewers
wishes: Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly

stops.summary: Tabelog Top 100 tonkatsu within ten months of opening: the hangover-proof lunch.
stops.story: Gabuu made Tabelog's Tonkatsu Top 100 within 10 months of opening, which in Tokyo's tonkatsu scene is basically a speed record. Thick, juicy cutlets, crunchy panko, and exactly the base layer you need for a day that ends at Round1. Highly rated on Tabelog; see the link.
how: Head to the Ueno 1号店; lunch opens at 11:30, walk-in only.
Get in the line as soon as you arrive and expect to sit 4+4.
After, walk to Akihabara for the JR Yamanote line to Yurakucho: 29 min door to door, ¥160, or a 12 min taxi.
tips: Closing days are not published (they point to Instagram): check their Instagram before you go.
Lunch runs 11:30–15:00, so a slow Daitoryo round won't kill the plan, but the line grows.
stops.booking: Walk-in at lunch (dinner bookable on Tabelog only)
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: Twelve floors of Japanese stationery: the cheapest, lightest souvenirs you will buy all trip.
stops.story: Itoya is a vertical stationery obsession in the middle of Ginza: New Year cards, washi paper and fountain pens stacked floor after floor. Everything here weighs nothing and packs flat, which matters when the suitcases already left for Haneda yesterday.
how: Ride to the top and work down.
Hit the New Year cards and washi for gifts.
Walk 8 min down Chuo-dori to Ginza Komatsu for Dover Street Market.
tips: Your suitcases are already with Yamato heading to Haneda: buy only what fits your carry-on.
Show your passport at the till if one person's haul clears the tax-free minimum.

stops.summary: Comme des Garçons, Supreme-adjacent drops and archive labels: Ginza's streetwear temple.
stops.story: Dover Street Market Ginza is Rei Kawakubo's multi-floor fever dream: Comme des Garçons lines next to archive labels and drops that never make it to your country. Even if you buy nothing, it is the most art-gallery shop in Tokyo.
how: Start at the top and work down the stairwells.
Look for the Japan-only CDG lines.
UNIQLO's flagship is next door.
tips: Pay on your own passport so the tax-free refund lands on your own card.
Don't pool purchases across people on one receipt: the refund is per person.
wishes: Streetwear, sneakers and vintage (Harajuku, Koenji, Shimokitazawa, Ameyoko, Amerikamura), Don Quijote and tax-free hauls

stops.summary: The 12-floor UNIQLO flagship: Japan-only UT collabs and Heattech for the long flight.
stops.story: This is UNIQLO's global flagship, a 12-floor tower of every colourway and the Japan-only UT collab tees you cannot get back home. Grab Heattech now: Shiba Park at sunset in late December is properly cold.
how: Go straight for the UT floor and the Japan-only collabs.
Pay per person on your own passport at the tax-free register.
Then Hibiya line to Hibiya and Mita line to Onarimon: 30 min door to door, ¥290, or an 11 min taxi.
tips: Put the Heattech on before Shiba Park, not after.
Keep every receipt in your carry-on for the Haneda kiosk tomorrow.
wishes: Streetwear, sneakers and vintage (Harajuku, Koenji, Shimokitazawa, Ameyoko, Amerikamura), Don Quijote and tax-free hauls

stops.summary: Free sunset under Tokyo Tower: temple gate, rows of jizō, then the tower lights flick on.
stops.story: Zōjō-ji's huge Sanmon gate frames Tokyo Tower like someone planned it, and behind the hall rows of small stone jizō in red bonnets and pinwheels sit in the cold. Sunset is around 16:30 in late December, then the tower lights up orange against a dark sky. No tower ticket, no queue, best group photo of the trip.
how: Enter through the Sanmon gate and walk past the main hall to the jizō rows.
Move into Shiba Park for the tower-and-sunset shot.
Stay until the lights come on, then head for Gonpachi.
tips: The main hall shuts at 17:30; see it first.
To Gonpachi it is 43 min by train or 11 min by taxi: take two taxis.
Bare trees and early dark this time of year; bring the layers.
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country
Legendary, not generic: nothing only there because it is on page one of every Tokyo or Kyoto itinerary, and no sit-down sightseeing filler between the big moments

stops.summary: The 'Kill Bill' izakaya: farewell dinner for 8 at one table in a two-storey wooden hall.
stops.story: Gonpachi is the wooden, lantern-lit hall that inspired the Crazy 88 fight in Kill Bill, and it still feels like a set. Eight of you at one table, sake raised, two weeks of chaos retold in two hours. This is the farewell toast.
how: Book by the party form or phone (050-5443-1691, reservations 11:30-22:00): online only takes up to 7.
Ask for 2F, overlooking the hall.
One bill; the seat is yours for 2 hours.
After, two taxis to DiverCity: 18 min, against 63 min and three changes by train.
tips: There is a ¥1,650 per person minimum after 17:00, which you will clear easily.
Drinking age is 20 and they can ask: passports on you.
Grab a photo on the stairs before you leave.
stops.booking: Party form, email or phone 050-5443-1691; online takes only up to 7
wishes: Everyone stays together; every booking is for 8 at the same table or private room (8名で、同じテーブル/個室)

stops.summary: Last night in Japan: Spocha, bowling, karaoke and the arcade till 3. Hours unverified: check.
stops.story: Round1 Stadium is the indoor-everything megaplex: Spocha's batting cages, roller skates and courts, plus bowling, karaoke booths and floors of arcade. Ending the trip here, at 3am, sweaty and hoarse, is the whole point. This is deliberate short night number two.
how: Check DiverCity's year-end hours on the Round1 page before you go: unverified.
Show official ID with your age for bowling and karaoke; passports work.
Get two taxis home to Garfield House when you're done.
tips: Year-end can change prices and hours; the Spocha price after 20:00 also changed this year, so confirm at the counter.
The Spocha student price needs a student ID card: bring it if you have one.
Under-20s can be turned away under night rules: everyone carries the original passport.
stops.hours: Normally Mon–Thu 8:00–6:00; year-end hours unverified, check
wishes: At most two deliberate nights under 4 hours' sleep; any early start after a late night needs a reason (rope-drop at USJ, first light at Fushimi Inari)
Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly
